features.name: Create and import recovery formats
features.summary: Create a new BIP39 wallet or import supported BIP39, Electrum and aezeed recovery material. Validation and signing happen on the device. Electrum and aezeed imports are Bitcoin-only and need manual recovery backups.

features.name: Password-encrypted iCloud backup
features.summary: Back up eligible wallets as encrypted .oathbackup files. Restore with the file and its separate backup password. Electrum and aezeed require manual recovery backups.

features.name: 57 app localizations
features.summary: Oath is available in 57 app localizations, with right-to-left layouts, local number formats and BIP39 word lists.

features.name: Open source, with a documented review scope
features.summary: The full source code is public on GitHub at https://github.com/devdasx/oath-wallet. The published release includes its security model, verification record and reporting policy. Public source is available for review; it does not establish an independent audit or a verified match to the App Store binary.

features.name: Bitcoin address options
features.summary: Compatible Bitcoin wallets support Taproot, Native SegWit, nested SegWit and Legacy, depending on the imported material. Capabilities vary by network. Oath 4.1.14 does not support Silent Payments receiving or discovery; see the Silent Payments guide before relying on that feature.

features.name: EVM Access
features.summary: A tool that shows discovered token approvals (web3 permissions) on supported EVM networks and lets the user submit supported revocation transactions. Revoking is an on-chain transaction with a network fee shown before confirming.

features.name: Your display currency
features.summary: Choose from the app’s supported display currencies. Values are estimates based on available exchange-rate data.

features.name: Available market prices
features.summary: See available price quotes for supported assets. Quotes can be delayed or unavailable; displayed fiat values are estimates.

faq.q: How do I create a wallet?
faq.a: Open Oath and tap “Create a new wallet”. Your keys are generated on your iPhone, then you’ll back up your recovery phrase. Creating a local wallet needs no Oath account or email.

faq.q: Can I import a wallet from another app?
faq.a: Yes. Choose Import wallet and use the original BIP39, Electrum or aezeed format with any required passphrase. Electrum and aezeed restore supported Bitcoin accounts. Private keys use a separate import with the matching network. Compare a known public address before moving funds.

faq.q: Can I create my own recovery phrase with dice?
faq.a: The 4.1.14 source creates standard wallets with a 12-word BIP39 phrase. The earlier dice, coin-flip and typed-digit creation controls are not included in this release.

faq.q: What if I lose my iPhone?
faq.a: Install Oath on a compatible iPhone or iPad and use the correct recovery phrase and any extra passphrase, or an existing encrypted iCloud backup with its backup password. Your funds live on the blockchain, not on your phone.

faq.q: Can Oath recover my recovery phrase?
faq.a: No. Recovery material is protected locally in the app, not held by Oath support. Keep your own recovery backup; support cannot replace missing words, keys or passwords.

faq.q: How does backup password restore work?
faq.a: Eligible iCloud backups need both the .oathbackup file and the separate password used to encrypt it. The app passcode or Apple Account access alone cannot decrypt it. Electrum and aezeed wallets need manual recovery material in 4.1.14.

faq.q: Is a backup password a replacement for my recovery phrase?
faq.a: Eligible iCloud backups need both the .oathbackup file and the separate password used to encrypt it. The app passcode or Apple Account access alone cannot decrypt it. Electrum and aezeed wallets need manual recovery material in 4.1.14.

faq.q: Why is my transaction pending?
faq.a: Transactions confirm when the network includes them. Busy networks take longer. You can see the status and the fee you paid in the transaction details.

faq.q: What are network fees?
faq.a: Fees go to the network, not to Oath. A network-fee estimate is shown before you confirm; the final fee can depend on the network and transaction.

faq.q: Which address type should I use for Bitcoin?
faq.a: Native SegWit (bc1q) and Taproot (bc1p) are efficient Bitcoin address options. The best choice depends on sender compatibility and how your coins will be spent. Nested SegWit and Legacy are also available where supported by the imported material. Silent Payments receiving and discovery are not supported in 4.1.14.

faq.q: Someone from “Oath support” asked for my phrase.
faq.a: That is a scam. Oath will never ask for your recovery phrase, private key or passkey. Don’t reply, and forward the message to care@oathwallet.org.

faq.q: Is Oath open source?
faq.a: Yes. The full source is published on GitHub at github.com/devdasx/oath-wallet, with a current security model, release verification record and security policy. Public source does not establish an independent audit or a verified match to the App Store binary.

faq.q: What is EVM Access?
faq.a: A tool that shows discovered token approvals on supported EVM networks. Revoke a supported permission with an on-chain transaction; a network fee applies.

faq.q: Does revoking an approval cost a fee?
faq.a: Yes, a small network fee, because revoking is an on-chain transaction. Oath shows it before you confirm.

faq.q: What is a self-custody crypto wallet?
faq.a: A self-custody, or non-custodial, wallet lets you authorize transactions with your wallet’s private keys. The crypto remains recorded on its blockchain. Your wallet helps you manage the credentials and addresses used to access it. Keeping a usable recovery method is your responsibility.

faq.q: How is a wallet different from an exchange account?
faq.a: With a custodial exchange account, the provider controls the withdrawal keys. With self-custody, you manage the signing credentials. This removes reliance on an exchange to approve a withdrawal, but it also means a forgotten recovery phrase, a malicious approval or a mistaken transfer can cause permanent loss.

faq.q: Can I use Oath for Bitcoin and other crypto on iPhone?
faq.a: Oath Wallet is available for iPhone and iPad. Choose the asset and network in the app before sharing a receiving address. A matching coin name or address format does not mean two networks are interchangeable. Available actions depend on your app version, network and wallet type.

faq.q: What happens if I lose my phone?
faq.a: Recovery depends on the backup you prepared before the loss. A recovery phrase may also require its separate BIP-39 passphrase. Oath’s optional iCloud recovery needs the encrypted backup and the backup password. Check your recovery method before relying on it, and never share recovery words with support.

faq.q: Is Oath free, and why do transfers have fees?
faq.a: Oath is free to download from the App Store. Blockchain transfers can require network fees, account reserves or activation costs. These vary by network and conditions. Review the asset, destination, network and fee before confirming; an on-chain transfer generally cannot be reversed.

faq.q: Does open source mean a wallet has been audited?
faq.a: Public code lets people inspect an implementation. It does not by itself establish an independent security audit or prove that the app installed on a phone matches that code. Oath publishes its source-review scope and limitations so you can check the evidence behind a claim.

articles.title: Krisis Seed Lemah Coldcard: Kompleksitas Tidak Sama dengan Keamanan

articles.title: Coldcards Krise um schwache Seeds: Komplexität ist nicht gleich Sicherheit

articles.title: A crise das sementes fracas da Coldcard: complexidade não é o mesmo que segurança
articles.excerpt: O incidente da Coldcard em 2026 não comprometeu remotamente os dispositivos. Ele expôs algo mais fundamental: um invólucro sofisticado não pode proteger uma semente que era previsível desde sua criação.

articles.title: Coldcard’ın Zayıf Tohum Krizi: Karmaşıklık Güvenlikle Aynı Şey Değildir
articles.excerpt: 2026’daki Coldcard vakasında cihazlar uzaktan ele geçirilmedi. Vaka, daha temel bir gerçeği açığa çıkardı: Gelişmiş bir muhafaza, oluşturulduğu anda öngörülebilir olan bir tohumu koruyamaz.

articles.title: أزمة البذور الضعيفة في Coldcard: التعقيد ليس مرادفًا للأمن

articles.title: Khủng hoảng seed yếu của Coldcard: Phức tạp không đồng nghĩa với bảo mật

source_correspondence.statement: Oath Wallet 4.1.14 (98) is built from public source commit v4.1.14. Its release record separates source checks, host tests, compilation and App Store Connect delivery. Provider configuration and Apple signing are supplied through encrypted deployment secrets and excluded from Git. Version 4.1.14 (98) is a public source release. Its App Store Connect upload-only workflow was cancelled before upload at the maintainer’s request; it was not submitted for review. See its release record for delivery evidence.
source_correspondence.independent_verification: This statement is distinct from an independently reproduced, byte-for-byte comparison of an App Store download. This update supplies no new binary comparison, independent reproducibility report, or security audit.
